title: Elabora course (course.json)
description: Root file of an Elabora course project. It lists the sections and the order of screens, declares variables, the theme, navigation, completion and tracking rules. Screens live in screens/<id>.json, the validated plan in plan.json.

format.description: Format identifier and version. Always "elabora/0.1" for this version of the specification. Older courses are migrated by elabora migrate (Elabora reads them migrated in memory meanwhile).

id.description: Stable course identifier. Used for the SCORM manifest identifiers: changing it makes LMSs treat the package as a different course.

title.description: Course title shown to learners and in the LMS.

description.description: Short description for the LMS catalogue.

language.description: Language of the content. Selects the player labels (fr and en are built in).

version.description: Content version of the course. Increase it at every delivery.

durationMinutes.description: Typical learner duration, written into the SCORM manifest metadata.

sections.description: Ordered sections (modules) of the course. Each lists the ids of its screens, in learner order. Every screen must appear exactly once.

variables.description: Course variables, readable and writable by events. Persisted variables are saved in the learner's suspend data, so their size counts against the LMS budget.

speakers.description: The voices of the course's narration (screen narration lines name them): the name shown in captions and in the transcript, and the voice that speaks each language.

narration.description: Defaults of the course's narrated screens (each screen's narration may say otherwise).

seek.description: How far learners may move in their timeline (screen narration.seek).

pronunciations.description: How generated voices say words of the whole course (an acronym, a reference, a name), by language: each language has its own list, never translated.

ignored.description: Warnings the author looked at and chose to ignore (docs/decisions.md D31): the validator marks the finding of that code with that key ignored, and it counts no more. A key names what the finding is about and a fingerprint of what was found (a swallowed word: the line, the word and its take's audio), so a finding that changes (another take) comes back. Written by the editor (ignore_findings), not by update_course; unlike plan waivers, nobody approves them, and the proof dossier says them ignored by the author. Never shipped in packages.

code.description: The code of the finding ignored: a warning or an information, never an error.

key.description: The finding's key (Diagnostic.key): what it is about, then @ and the fingerprint of what was found.

presentation.description: How screens are presented. scroll: a document per screen (default); steps appear one below the other. slides: every screen is one view that should fit the window (checked by elabora fit and elabora test at the fit sizes); steps appear in their reserved place. Sizes are in px at the reference window (1600×900) and follow the size classes of the player (1rem is 14 px at 1280×720).

contentWidth.description: Width of the reading column (blocks of width full), in px at the reference window; emitted in rem, so it follows the size classes.

wideWidth.description: Width of wide blocks and of the screen, in px at the reference window; emitted in rem.

fit.description: Window sizes (width x height, CSS px, inside the LMS frame) where a slide must fit without scrolling. reference: the size the course is designed for; an overflow there is a warning (W_SLIDE_OVERFLOW). minimum: the smallest supported size; slides may scroll there and an overflow is only reported (I_SLIDE_OVERFLOW_MINIMUM). Below it, and on phones, slides read as a scrolling page.

mode.description: linear: Previous/Next only. free: learners can also jump to any screen from the menu.

lockUntilComplete.description: If true, Next stays disabled until the current screen is complete.

showMenu.description: Show the list of sections and screens.

footer.description: Where the Previous and Next buttons are. sticky: a bar at the bottom of the window. end: at the end of the page, after its content (scroll presentation, like the end of a lesson in Rise); in slides the page ends with the window, so both look alike.

completion.description: How the course reports completion and success to the LMS. The final status is sent once, when it is decided (never only at exit).

reportAs.description: Status pair reported in SCORM 1.2 cmi.core.lesson_status, as in Storyline. completed-incomplete: completed when all required screens are complete. passed-incomplete: passed when required screens are complete and the score reaches masteryScore. passed-failed: passed or failed once every scored item is answered. completed-failed: completed when required screens are complete, failed if the score is below masteryScore.

masteryScore.description: Passing score in percent. Required for every reportAs except completed-incomplete. Written to the manifest as adlcp:masteryscore.

exitAfterCompletion.description: Value of cmi.core.exit once the course is complete. suspend keeps resume data for review; normal ends the attempt. Never logout (SuccessFactors logs the learner out).

recordInteractions.description: Write quiz, decision and free-object answers to cmi.interactions, linked to plan objectives.

heartbeatSeconds.description: Periodic commit of session time while the course is open (0 disables). Keeps long sessions alive in LMSs that expire them.

delivery.description: How the SCORM package is delivered.

mediaQuality.description: Preset of the video, audio and raster images shipped in the package (elabora build --media-quality overrides it for one build). high: the masters the project keeps (video H.264 long side ≤ 1920, CRF 21, ≤ 8 Mb/s, AAC 160 kb/s; audio AAC 160 kb/s; images long side ≤ 3200, WebP q 88). medium: renditions encoded from the masters (video ≤ 1280, CRF 24, ≤ 4 Mb/s, AAC 128 kb/s; audio AAC 128 kb/s; images ≤ 2400, q 80). low: smaller renditions for LMSs with tight size limits (video ≤ 854, CRF 27, ≤ 1.5 Mb/s, ≤ 30 fps, AAC 96 kb/s; audio AAC 96 kb/s; images ≤ 1600, q 72). A rendition that would be larger than its master ships the master; SVG images are never re-encoded. E_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE says what the lower presets would weigh.

lms.description: The LMS the course is delivered to: ids of LMS profiles (elabora profiles lists them). elabora build, validate and test target them when no --profile is given: the package must fit their limits (size, files, suspend data). Without it the course targets an unknown LMS: the strictest documented behaviour, and package limits only warn, naming the LMSs that would refuse the package.

ui.description: Overrides for player labels, keyed by label id (see docs). Example: {"next": "Continuer"}.

translationOf.description: Set by elabora translate build: this course is the translation of another (its id, version and language). Generated: edit the source course and its translations/<lang>.xlf.

name.description: The name learners read in captions and in the transcript (Leïla, Narrator).

voices.description: The voice that speaks each language, keyed by language tag (fr, en, fr-CA): the voice tools generate the lines of this speaker with it, and a generated line made with another voice is out of date.

provider.description: The voice tool that makes it (a local model, a voice service).

voice.description: The provider's id of the voice.

name.description: The voice's name as its provider gives it, for a voice service whose voices Elabora does not list itself (ElevenLabs): shown to authors without asking the service. Information only: never makes a line out of date.

settings.description: What the provider needs besides the voice (speed, style…), as it defines it. ElevenLabs: model (eleven_v4 by default), stability and similarity (0 to 1).

variable.description: A course variable. Strings need maxLength so the suspend data budget can be computed.

default.description: Initial value; must match the type.

options.description: Allowed values of a choice variable.

persist.description: Save in suspend data so the value survives a relaunch.

theme.description: Visual identity. tokens: the client charter (checked for contrast). custom: extra named values (colours, sizes) exposed as CSS variables and to free objects. stylesheet: free CSS for the whole course (cascade layer elabora.theme; its top-level @layer overrides blocks: elabora.overrides). cascade: where the theme sits among the cascade layers. fonts: embedded font files. styles: named styles that authors can pick per block or screen. Text never lives here: it stays in blocks.

cascade.description: Order of the cascade layers (docs/decisions.md D32). components-over-theme (what elabora init writes): the player, the theme's rules (the course's defaults), the component stylesheets, then the theme's top-level @layer overrides { … } blocks (what it overrides in components on purpose). theme-over-components: the order before 13 October 2026, the theme after the components, which it overrides whatever the specificity; what a course without cascade gets, so that it keeps its look. elabora theme upgrade moves a course from the second to the first without changing its look.

color.primary.description: Main brand colour: buttons, progress, headings accents.

font.body.description: CSS font stack for text. Only system or embedded fonts: no external font URL.

custom.description: Extra design tokens, for example {"color.blueprint": "#0F2A47", "space.section": "72px"}. Each becomes the CSS variable --t-<name with dots as hyphens> (--t-color-blueprint) in the player and in free objects, and can be bound to free-object props with x-token. Editors show them next to the charter tokens.

stylesheet.description: Free CSS for the course, in theme/ (cascade layer elabora.theme, after the player and the components). Style the documented DOM contract (docs/design.md): data-screen, data-layout, data-type, data-component, data-style, .t-* classes, --t-* variables. url() must point to files inside the course (theme/ for fonts and textures, assets/ for generated images); no @import, no external URL. Use var(--t-…) for colours so a charter change propagates.

fonts.description: Embedded fonts (WOFF2 or WOFF files in theme/). The player declares them with @font-face and passes them to free objects; reference the family in font.body / font.heading or in the stylesheet. Check the font licence allows embedding (OFL fonts do). A face split into subset files (latin, latin-ext) is one entry per file, each with its unicodeRange.

weight.description: Weight or weight range of a variable font, for example "100 900".

unicodeRange.description: The characters the file holds, as a CSS unicode-range, for example "U+0100-02BA,U+1E00-1E9F" (the latin-ext subset of a font): the browser downloads the file only for pages that use one of them. Default: every character.

styles.description: Named styles declared by the theme, per type (a built-in type, a course component id, or "screen"), with a one-line description for editors: {"callout": {"rule": "Key rule on a dark card"}}. Blocks and screens pick one with style; the player adds data-style and the class t-s-<name>; the stylesheet styles it. Styles declared for a type also apply to its forks. Components can declare their own styles in component.json. (Not to be confused with the callout prop variant: info, tip, warning, important.)

effects.description: Effects of the theme for timed blocks (block timing.in and timing.out effect), each with a one-line description for editors: {"pop": "Grows a little past its size, then settles"}. The stylesheet defines @keyframes t-fx-<name> (how the block comes) and may define @keyframes t-fx-<name>-out (how it goes; default: the first one played backwards). The player plays them at the timeline's time, as the built-in effects (none, fade, rise, slide, zoom, wipe, draw, whose names are taken). Keep them relative to the block (transform, opacity, clip-path, filter): never move the layout, never flash (WCAG 2.3.1).

backdrop.description: Decorative background behind every screen. Decoration only: it carries no information, takes no focus and is hidden from screen readers (a scene that teaches is a free-object block). layers: empty elements behind the course that the stylesheet paints and animates (.t-backdrop-layer[data-layer="far"]); the backdrop element carries data-screen, data-section, data-step and data-variant, so the stylesheet can react to where the learner is. object: a decorative free object (pedagogicalRole "decoration") mounted once behind the course for the whole session, given the same context. Under reduced motion CSS animations stop and the object shows still frames; on a slow machine the object freezes. Text over a backdrop must stay readable: elabora fit measures its contrast against the pixels behind it (W_TEXT_CONTRAST_MEASURED).

layers.description: Layer names, back to front: <div class="t-backdrop-layer" data-layer="<name>"> each.

object.description: Decorative free object of objects/<id>/ (pedagogicalRole decoration) and its prop values.

props.description: Prop values, checked against the manifest.

variants.description: Named variants a screen can pick with backdrop, each with a one-line description for editors: {"dim": "Darker sky behind dense screens"}. The stylesheet styles .t-backdrop[data-variant=…]; the object receives the variant.
